{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZboyzw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDC6fQ", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 53, "title": "Implement 8253 mode-3 count-only rewrites at half-cycle boundaries", "body": "## Problem

Writing a replacement divisor to an active mode-3 counter prematurely restarts its phase. This changes timer IRQ timing and beeper OUT polarity when guest software updates the count without writing another control word.

At baseline `e4f90a325dff690e962c5a952dccee865c5861a7`, [Counter::write](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e4f90a325dff690e962c5a952dccee865c5861a7/src/devices.rs#L195) replaces `reload` and sets `load_pending` for every completed mode-3 write. `tick_mode3` subsequently resets the phase to zero. The source comment and [hardware contract](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e4f90a325dff690e962c5a952dccee865c5861a7/docs/hardware.md#L469) explicitly leave active mode-3 rewrites outstanding.

## Expected outcome

Implement count-only replacement for binary mode 3, encodings 3/7, divisors 2–65,536, with the existing GATE-high model. Apply it to all three counters through both timer port banks on VM and Ap.

The hardware contract is:

- A complete replacement preserves the active count and OUT sequence through the current half-cycle. At its terminal boundary, OUT toggles and the replacement loads for the next half-cycle, without an extra initial-load clock.
- Paired writes become complete only after the MSB. An unfinished pair does not restart or stop an established count. The latest completed replacement available before the boundary supplies the reload.
- Preserve the programmed access format, ordinary completed latch snapshots, and the established 8253 even/odd count sequences. Initial programming still has its separate load clock; a fresh mode word or Machine reset cancels replacement state.

[Intel’s 8253/8253-5 datasheet, Mode 3 and Read/Write Procedure](https://web.cecs.pdx.edu/~mpj/llp/references/8253.pdf) describes terminal-count toggling/full-count reloading and byte sequencing. The half-cycle interpretation is cross-checked against the explicit replacement rule in [Intel’s 8254 datasheet, Mode 3, printed pp. 12–13](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/23wi-cs212/pintos/specs/8254.pdf#page=12). Use that reference for reload timing while retaining the 8253’s distinct odd-count readback behavior.

Only actual OUT0 low-to-high transitions request IRQ0. Falling transitions and held levels do not generate requests, consistent with [Intel’s 8259A edge-triggered input contract, printed p. 17](https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse451/25wi/documentation/8259A.pdf#page=17). Retain the existing PIC request-latching abstraction and bounded scheduler arithmetic.

Scope excludes other PIT modes, external GATE/retriggering, BCD, divisor-1 policy, 8254 read-back commands, PIC electrical/spurious-interrupt modeling, audio resampling changes, and unrelated refactoring.

## Context and reproduction

The [existing mode-3 tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/e4f90a325dff690e962c5a952dccee865c5861a7/tests/pit.rs#L444) cover initial programming, steady count/OUT traces, access forms, latches, batching, interrupts and reset. Their replacement scenarios use fresh mode words; the original guest probe also reprograms the mode before its second divisor. They do not establish count-only replacement behavior.

A source-derived reproduction using the existing `Clock` test helper is:

1. Program channel 0 with control word `16h` and divisor 8.
2. Advance through the load clock and two decrement clocks: states are `(8,H)`, `(6,H)`, `(4,H)`.
3. Write divisor 6 without another control word.
4. The next states must be `(2,H)`, `(6,L)`, `(4,L)`, `(2,L)`, `(6,H)`, with a rising-edge indication only on the last transition. Current source instead loads `(6,H)` on the first following clock.

This reproduction is derived from source and the documented contract; the evaluator did not execute it.

Issue #47 implemented initial/steady mode 3 and explicitly deferred this behavior. Issue #51/PR #52 implemented mode-0 rewrites, a different lifecycle. The supplied history contains no open Issue duplicating this scope.

Project progress: the supplied history and local HEAD record PR #52 merged at this baseline. The [Coordinator’s PR report](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/52) reports 12 focused mode-0 rewrite passes, 42 PIT passes, 202 native integration passes, and 78 production-Wasm browser passes with no skips. Browser execution used documented alternate ports after a port conflict. These are attributed reports; remote CI and independent review evidence were not supplied. No runtime validation was repeated by this evaluator.

All 26 inventory scopes and statuses remain unchanged:

- **Partial:** cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, bios, lio, integration.
- **Unimplemented:** paging, fpu, rtc.
- **Implemented, unverified:** ide, grcg, pcm86.

PIT remains partial after this Issue. Remaining work includes modes 1/4/5, external GATE/retriggering, BCD, mode-2/3 divisor-1 behavior, fuller latch/access sequencing, non-mode-3 beeper behavior and audio sampling across large scheduler batches. Protected execution, paging and basic FPU remain required project goals. Limited probes and six-game reports do not establish full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

The resident Coordinator owns implementation, builds, test execution and review.

- [ ] Add focused `mode3_rewrite_` Rust tests in `tests/pit.rs`. Record a baseline failure demonstrating premature reload, then passing results with the implementation. Include the explicit reproduction above and an independently specified low-half rewrite trace.
- [ ] Cover replacements during both halves, immediately before and after terminal boundaries, even-to-odd and odd-to-even changes, repeated completed replacements, and an unfinished paired write spanning half-cycle boundaries. Exercise all channels, encodings 3/7, LSB/MSB/paired access forms, and representable boundary values including 2, 3, 65,535 and encoded zero. Avoid assertions about undefined initial pre-load readback.
- [ ] Verify count reads/latches, channel isolation, fresh-mode cancellation and Machine reset with a deferred replacement pending. Preserve initial-load and mode-0/2 behavior.
- [ ] Compare single-clock advancement with irregular batches spanning the old half-cycle, replacement boundary and subsequent periods. Compare final state, future behavior, fractional clock remainder and aggregated rising edges. Include zero advancement and split/unsplit `u32::MAX` scheduler advancement; production advancement must remain bounded without a loop per elapsed clock.
- [ ] Exercise both profiles and both port banks through `Bus`: writes alone cause no OUT transition; falling boundaries cause no IRQ0; natural rising boundaries reach IRR with masks/ISR/EOI respected. Confirm IF-clear/HLT deferral and subsequent handler/IRET delivery. Check channel-1 beeper sample polarity before and after a deferred replacement without changing mixer timing or queue limits.
- [ ] Add a separate original MIT source-built guest probe, offline preparation script and checked provenance manifest. Pin source/boot/image hashes, assembly command, result bytes/guards and a maximum 2,000,000-slot budget per boot. The guest must distinguish deferred replacement from immediate restart using count latches and service natural IRQ0 with ISR/EOI/IRET checks. Hosts only load, step, reset and inspect; they must not inject IRQs or results. Avoid counter reads between paired write bytes.
- [ ] Run the identical probe natively and through production-release Wasm on VM/Ap, before/after reset, at both browser roots `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Require exact manifest results/guards, PASS without FAIL/core/browser errors, unchanged disk bytes and the fixed execution budget. Prepare the probe in CI before acceptance suites; retain existing probes and manifests.
- [ ] After preparing the legal existing fixtures and new probe, run `cargo test --locked --test pit mode3_rewrite_`, `cargo test --locked --test pit`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check`, and `npm test`. Preserve existing PIT/PIC/BIOS timer/CPU-shadow, DOS/application, VM and game assertions and budgets. Report exact commands, failures, skips and any equivalent alternate-port browser configuration. Use original/licensed acceptance assets with explicit provenance; acquire no commercial ROMs or guest software.
- [ ] Update the bounded hardware contract, reproduction instructions, fixture provenance and validation record with actual evidence. Keep PIT partial and retain every fixed inventory category and remaining scope. Obtain a pre-merge review resolving all agent-fixable findings against these criteria.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
